subject: [PATCH v5 01/11] mm, swap: add virtual swap device infrastructure

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about vswap not implementing an ordinary swap device's behavior, explaining that it uses virtualization to reduce overhead when indirection is not needed. The author acknowledges this as a necessary condition for non-zswap inter-tier transfer but notes it's not sufficient and still under investigation.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 2:14 PM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Vswap does not have that, because vswap is not an ordinary swap
> device. It's implementing the concept of virtualization (the "V" in
> VFS, if you want to make that analogy), made optional to reduce
> overhead when indirection is not needed. That gives you all the
> machinery you need for backend transfer:

... for zswap/compression backend.

It's a necessary condition for non-zswap inter-tier transfer, but not
sufficient. So it's not a solved problem quite there yet (and I don't
know if it can become worth the squeeze, as the data becomes
increasingly colder as you move down the tier).

> layer, where you can update the backend, without having to go and
> chase down all the external references - no PTE walk needed.

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This patch introduces the virtual swap device infrastructure, allowing for dynamic allocation of swap clusters and enabling the creation of a virtual swap device that can be used by vswap. The device is capped at approximately 8 TiB in size and uses a 64-bit architecture. It includes a dynamic cluster allocator and resolves swap entries' clusters under RCU. The patch also introduces a kernel parameter 'vswap=' to control the routing of vswap paths, defaulting to CONFIG_VSWAP_DEFAULT_ON. The device is not swappable or removable and can be used by vswap-aware paths in subsequent patches.
